title: Timeline and character grid
subject: English
unit: Summer 2: Biographies: conviction, justice and legacy
source: Written for english/y7 lesson 66 (Timeline and character grid (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 66: Biography: Umar ibn al-Khattab (عمر بن الخطاب), leadership and justice. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

timeline.label: c. 584 CE
timeline.text: Born in Makkah, of the Quraysh tribe

timeline.label: c. 616 CE
timeline.text: Accepts Islam; Muslims gain strength in Makkah

timeline.label: 634 CE (13 AH)
timeline.text: Becomes the second caliph after Abu Bakr

timeline.label: c. 638 CE
timeline.text: Sets the Islamic calendar from the Hijrah; Jerusalem comes under Muslim rule

timeline.label: 644 CE (23 AH)
timeline.text: Dies in Madinah; buried beside the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr

head: What he did
Quality it shows
rows: set up a register (diwan) so people received regular support from the treasury
lived simply, in plain and patched clothes, as ruler of a vast state
asked his governors to account for their wealth

model.title: How does the biography present Umar's leadership?

parts.text: Evidence: he 'lived simply... as ruler of a vast state'
Technique: contrast between power and simplicity
Zoom in: 'vast' stresses how much power he could have used for himself

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: The biography presents Umar's leadership as service: by contrasting the 'vast' state with his simple life, the writer shows that power did not change him.

keywords.def: a leader of the Muslim community after the Prophet ﷺ (khalifah)
fairness and giving everyone their right ('adl)
not thinking yourself better than others
Umar's title: the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood

questions.q: What does the title al-Faruq mean?
questions.a: the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood

questions.q: Give one achievement of his caliphate
questions.a: For example: the Islamic calendar from the Hijrah

questions.q: Core: complete the character grid: five facts, three qualities, evidence for each
Extend: write a PETZAAL Point and Evidence on how Umar is presented
questions.a: A Point with an embedded quotation

questions.q: Stretch: compare Umar's leadership with Prospero's in The Tempest
questions.a: For example: Umar uses power to serve; Prospero first uses it for control, then forgives

questions.q: Why might a ruler of a huge state choose patched clothes?
options: because he had no money at all
to stay humble and close to ordinary people
questions.a: C) to stay humble and close to ordinary people. Choosing simplicity while holding power shows humility and solidarity with the people.

questions.q: Umar set the Islamic calendar to start from...
One leadership quality Umar shows, with evidence
questions.a: For example: humility: he wore patched clothes as ruler
